page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers due to its burstable CPU allocation model. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests register at 1140.79 and 3253.57 respectively, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench scores reflect a constrained processing profile, with a single-core score of 910.0 and a multi-core score of 1988.0. Memory read bandwidth for large blocks is measured at 23.93 GB/sec, while database operations and Redis SET performance at 2.65 million operations per second also align with entry-level workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t3.xlarge offers a budget-friendly profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it utilizes a burstable CPU credit model, it is highly resource-dense and cost-effective for applications that remain idle or run at low baseline levels but require occasional performance bursts. This makes the instance suitable for development environments, code repositories, low-traffic web servers, and small database instances rather than sustained high-performance computing.
